label: October 26–November 01
title: “I Will Turn Their Mourning into Joy” —  Jeremiah 31

items.text: When sin or adversity has left our lives in ruins, we can rebuild and plant again through the Messiah. He brings a new covenant, where His law is written in our hearts, enabling us to truly be God’s people. The Lord promises, “I will turn their mourning into joy” when we seek Him.

In the midst of captivity and "lamentation, and bitter weeping," the Lord offers comfort and hope. He promises to establish a new and everlasting covenant with His people, where they will be His people and He will be their God. This covenant is written in our hearts.

Having God’s law written in our hearts means a deeper, more personal relationship with Him. It transforms our covenant relationship, changing us from the inside out as we strive to be His covenant people. He fulfills His promises to us as we keep ours to Him.

The Lord commanded Jeremiah to record his prophecies so they would have power to turn people away from evil. Pondering the scriptures can help us feel their power and strengthen our resolve to leave sin behind, just as they did for Jeremiah and Baruch.

The scriptures possess a remarkable power to inspire individuals to turn away from wickedness. Observing the varied reactions to Jeremiah's prophecies—from King Jehoiakim's destruction to Baruch's faithful recording—highlights the profound impact these sacred words can have on our hearts.

King Zedekiah’s wavering belief in Jeremiah demonstrates the consequences of not following God's prophets. Had he and his people heeded the prophet's counsel and kept the Lord's commandments, their destiny might have been vastly different, a lesson also seen in the Book of Mormon.

Being firm in following God's prophets requires faith and conviction. Comparing Zedekiah's choices with Lehi's obedience illustrates the critical difference between heeding divine counsel and rejecting it, ultimately impacting personal and collective destinies. The Lord's prophets guide us to safety and salvation.

Even when facing opposition and severe trials, like Jeremiah in the dungeon, we can be bold in standing up for what is right. Ebed-melech the Ethiopian showed courage by acting on the prophet's behalf, demonstrating that righteousness can prevail even in the darkest circumstances.

The example of Ebed-melech teaches us the importance of courage and compassion in defending righteousness. His bold actions in rescuing Jeremiah from the dungeon brought him a blessing from the Lord, showing that standing for truth is always rewarded. We too can follow his example.

The Lord promises to turn mourning into joy for His covenant people. Even amidst sorrow and repentance, His divine power offers solace and hope, transforming our deepest grief into lasting happiness. This promise is rooted in His everlasting covenant and His love for us.
